chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies, should she go out to the house of her father and her mother from her house if she so desires, so she observes the waiting period? So he (peace be upon him) said: If she so desires, she observes the waiting period in the house of her husband, and if she so desires, she observes the waiting period among her family, and she should not apply Kohl nor wear jewellery.
And she should not apply Kohl nor wear jewellery.

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The woman whose husband has died (widow)
key_terms.بَيْتِ زَوْجِهَا: The house of her husband (marital home)

ai.seo_question: Where should a widow observe her waiting period after her husband's death according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic flexibility regarding the location of the widow's waiting period (Iddah), affirming her right to choose between her marital home or her parents' residence. It further specifies the behavioral constraints during this time, notably the prohibition of applying kohl and wearing jewelry, which aligns with the broader Shia emphasis on modesty and mourning rituals. This ruling underscores the balance between legal obligation and personal agency in post-marital transitions within Shia fiqh.
